clue.text: Backing your paintings I support making a free choice

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of pieces is set down from the end to the start

parts.note: art is a collective word for paintings
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone props up a friend's art collection while choosing freely what to hang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns the whole run YR + ART + I + BRA, which reads YRARTIBRA forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arbitrary is settled by whim or personal choice rather than by any rule.

clue.text: Was in play about church, quietly received

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the others here

parts.note: to have acted is to have performed in a play
CE is the Church of England
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An actor in a church drama is greeted with hushed approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was in play' reads like a game, but it means performed on stage; 'about' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accepted has been taken in or welcomed, so received is a synonym.

clue.text: Wrongly bar Virginia's cheer for female singer

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of bar are put in a different order

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in the wrong place, heckling a bar in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' signals the rearrangement; the cheer is the feminine form, for a woman singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian audiences shout the feminine form of bravo to applaud a woman performer.

clue.text: One who certainly does not absorb the spirit of the age

definitions.text: One who certainly does not absorb the spirit of the age

parts.words: One who certainly does not absorb the spirit of the age
parts.note: the surface describes someone out of touch with modern times, but spirit is drink: this person never takes in alcohol at all

explanation.surface: A stick-in-the-mud who refuses to take on board current fashions and ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete teetotaller refuses every alcoholic spirit, of any age or vintage.

clue.text: Separate in the manner shown below

parts.note: as means in the way or manner of
under means below

explanation.surface: An instruction to set something apart in the way illustrated beneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Separate is an adverb here: torn asunder means torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or into pieces, the state of things separated.

clue.text: Yen I had to adopt pretty woman's language

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen
I'd is the contraction of I had
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A man with a yen for a pretty woman takes up her tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Germanic tongue historically spoken by Ashkenazi Jews.

clue.text: Arranged for a hairdo

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of for a are reordered

explanation.surface: A hairdresser has fixed things up for a customer's styling.
explanation.definitionFit: An afro is a rounded bushy hairstyle, a type of hairdo.

clue.text: Give early warning, as golfer's cry over hollow

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn others of a ball in flight
a token gesture is a hollow, empty one

explanation.surface: A golfer warns others with a shout over a hollow in the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' looks like a dip in the ground but is an adjective, a token or empty gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretoken is to presage or signal in advance.

clue.text: Cheer about day on street being first on the scene?

indicators.note: about puts the word for cheer round the abbreviation for day

parts.note: ole is a shout of encouragement in Spain

explanation.surface: Fans cheer on a big day in the street for whoever arrived earliest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first to arrive anywhere has been there longest.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever has been around longest arrived earliest, so is the most aged in that sense.

clue.text: Harrier at liberty to see terrorist?

parts.note: freedom means liberty
the Harrier is a British jump-jet fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: A hunting dog let off the lead goes to look for a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harrier' suggests a hound but is the warplane; the question mark flags that one side's terrorist is the other side's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla fighting a regime may be branded a terrorist by those in power.

clue.text: Church worker identifies monastic tune

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A church employee picks out a tune sung by monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong or Gregorian singing by monks is known by this name.

clue.text: Inferior bread one left out for mongrel?

parts.note: under means lower or inferior, as in an undersecretary

indicators.note: left out says the letter for one is dropped from bread

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Poor-quality bread with something missing is fed to a scruffy dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' takes A from BREAD, leaving BRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is of mixed or low breeding, so poorly bred describes it.

clue.text: Worked as a diver for Shell, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word for worked is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: to purl is to work a knitting stitch

explanation.surface: Someone was employed as an undersea diver for the oil company Shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' is knitting, a purl stitch; the definition describes a diver who fished for pearl shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers fished the seabed for oysters, collecting pearls and mother-of-pearl shell.

clue.text: medical complaint

annotationWithheld.why: the clue as held is only 'medical complaint (7)': the wordplay before it has been cut off and no reprint or search supplies it

clue.text: Sweet stick of Cherbourg kind possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Cherbourg kind can be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A stick of sweets of the sort sold in the French port of Cherbourg.
explanation.walkthrough: EDINBURGH ROCK is a crumbly, pastel-coloured Scottish confection sold in sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish confection is a soft, sugary candy made in short bars.

clue.text: Pathological neatness is almost unfeeling

indicators.note: almost says the word is loses its final letter
pathological suggests something disordered, so neatness is rearranged

explanation.surface: Obsessive tidiness is close to being heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is almost' gives I; 'Pathological' rearranges NEATNESS into NSENSATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensate means lacking sensation or sympathy, numb and callous.

clue.text: Everybody else has scope for facilities

parts.note: the rest means everybody else
room means scope or space to act

explanation.surface: Everyone else has opportunities to use the amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' is the euphemism for toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: The facilities is a polite term for a lavatory, as is this American term.

clue.text: Fail to make up your mind to put down the receiver?

definitions.text: Fail to make up your mind
definitions.meaning: to stay undecided between two sides
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods, and to sit on one is to put him down

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over whether to hang up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' suggests a telephone; it is a fence, a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying neutral in a dispute is idiomatically perching between two fields; literally, perching on a dealer in stolen goods.

clue.text: Sarnies cut for this woman

indicators.note: cut suggests sandwiches chopped up, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Sandwiches sliced up for a particular lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarnies is British slang for sandwiches; NERISSA is Portia's maid in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, borne by Portia's waiting-woman in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Looking guilty, kill wretch with rope?

parts.note: to hang is to kill with a rope
dog is a term of contempt for a wretched person

explanation.surface: A guilty-looking villain is executed on the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with rope' tells you which kind of killing is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog expression is shamefaced and sheepish, as if guilty.

clue.text: Boy securing success in snooker? Precisely

indicators.note: securing means the word for boy holds the snooker word inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is a successful shot sinking a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A young lad sinks a ball at the snooker table with great accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British cue game played on a large table.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is British slang for exactly right or accurate.

clue.text: Priest carrying woman's basket

indicators.note: carrying means the abbreviation for priest holds the name inside

parts.note: Annie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A clergyman carries a lady's shopping basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a basket slung on a pack animal or bicycle.

clue.text: Negative lecture shows lack of care

parts.note: lect. is a dictionary abbreviation for lecture

explanation.surface: A critical talk reveals someone's carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are abbreviations listed in dictionaries, so 'Negative lecture' is cut down rather than taken whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is failure to look after something properly.

clue.text: Break out and clean up with minimum of trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pure means clean or unsullied

indicators.note: minimum of trouble means only its smallest part, the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone escapes and tidies up with as little fuss as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PURE into ERUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst forth violently, like a volcano.

clue.text: Went across to find poetry in traditional surroundings

indicators.note: in places the poetry inside the abbreviation
surroundings says the word for traditional forms an enclosure

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz
verse means poetry

explanation.surface: A traveller crossed over to discover poems in an old-fashioned setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or through an area.

clue.text: See rot churned out about game

indicators.note: about puts the scrambled word round the game abbreviation
churned out says the letters of rot are mixed up

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: Someone notices rubbish produced by a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churned out' signals the rearrangement and 'about' the enclosure. TRURO is a cathedral city in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and Truro gives its name to the Cornish one.

clue.text: Want to prepare bread for report

indicators.note: for report means the bread-making word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: to knead is to work dough to make bread

explanation.surface: A baker wants to make bread for a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and need both mean a lack or requirement.

clue.text: Procedure behind goal possibly aroused mirth

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of goal could be arranged another way
aroused means the letters of mirth are stirred up

explanation.surface: A goal-celebration routine gets everyone laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GOAL as ALGO; 'aroused' turns MIRTH into RITHM.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step method for solving a problem.
